findings.reason: the s5 node cannot compute the failure-of-key result it is asked to report, so the plan should name a stable identity the router already holds (the run id read by `_request_identity`, router.py:1951/2075, or the run id header `identity_from_headers` returns) on the firing line, or drop the clause.
findings.text: the firing line names `the caller hint` as the only caller identity, and s5:57 decides the key's failure by "another firing from the same caller under a different key", but `RouterApp._caller_hint` builds that hint from `scope["client"]` as `f"{host}:{port}|{agent[:32]}"` (router.py:2100–2103) where the port is the client's ephemeral source port, and the retry the guard is designed to provoke arrives on a new connection because the guard takes the close form, which "deliberately sends no terminal chunk" so "the server drop[s] the connection" (router.py:2551–2556) — the firing and its retry therefore carry different hints and no second firing is ever attributed to the same caller

rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the changed line puts the guard's JSONL "beside the request receipts, in the directory the router's receipt sink writes" (`RouterApp._receipt_sink`, router.py:2596, defaulting to the lane document's directory, router.py:1747–1752), the fixtures and population-pass log sit under `~/.config/reckon/crew/reports/imas-ambix/a-tool-call-carries-no-model-markup/`, and s5's logs are "recorded beside the baseline"; none is a node-local temporary path or a session scratchpad.

rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the log line the commit added carries `the caller hint` as the caller's identity, and s5's key-failure clause pairs firings "from the same caller", but `_caller_hint` is `host:ephemeral-port|user-agent[:32]` (router.py:2100–2103) while the guard's own close form drops the connection (router.py:2551–2556), so the mechanism cannot produce the measure it is attached to.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — s3 carries one deliverable (the router guard, with the population pass as its measure and the `census.py` walk extraction as its means), and s5 carries one (confirm the guard is running on the serving router and count it), so neither gate carries two verdicts.
